goal: Install the weathernext package from /work/weathernext (pip install from the repo, as the notebook's install cell does) so the core flow of docs/weathernext2/wn2_demo.ipynb works on CPU: load fiddle config 'weathernext2/configs/WeatherNextCyclones_Mini', load weights weathernext2/params/WeatherNextCyclones_Mini_<2024.npz and the sample file weathernext2/dataset/source-hres_forecast_init-2024-10-07 00:00:00_res-1.0_levels-13_steps-04.nc from the public bucket dm_graphcast, then run the notebook's autoregressive ensemble rollout (fgn model, rollout.chunked_prediction_generator_multiple_runs). check: A standalone script downloads the public weights and steps-04 sample, runs a 2-member, 4-step Mini-model ensemble rollout on CPU, and checks finite, physically plausible 2m temperatures, nonzero ensemble spread, a 6h forecast close to the sample's target, and a written NetCDF output.

agent.final: h finite 2m temperatures between 207 and 317 K, about 0.3 K of ensemble spread, a 6h error of 0.73 K against the sample's target, and a NetCDF file written. Getting there took Python 3.12, dropping the unrelated `colabtools` PyPI package from setup.py, adding h5py and google-cloud-storage, and a small patch that switches the TPU-only attention kernel to the notebook's GPU fallback when not on TPU.

review.by: second review (independent check of the maintained passes against their raw logs)

patched_waived.why: Agent deleted the "colabtools" requirement pre-emptively (the PyPI name belongs to an unrelated third-party package) without trying the install. That package installs fine (pure wheel, no dependencies) and nothing imports it, so `pip install .` and the demo work unchanged. A reasonable supply-chain caution, but not needed for the demo.
patched_waived.evidence: google-deepmind/weathernext@f2f2c51 setup.py:34 "colabtools"; PyPI colabtools 0.0.1 ships colabtools-0.0.1-py3-none-any.whl, requires_dist None; commands.jsonl: `sed -i '/"colabtools",/d' setup.py` issued in the same command as the first install attempt

patched_waived.why: Agent made Transformer fall back from splash_mha (TPU Pallas kernel) to triblockdiag_mha on non-TPU backends. The notebook targets TPU/GPU (it switches only for gpu), so CPU is our sandbox, and the oracle already applies the same switch in the config (`if jax.default_backend() != "tpu": tk["attention_type"] = "triblockdiag_mha"`), so the repo edit was not needed to pass.
